supervision.transport: Atomic latest-state JSON file beside the unique recording folder; no preparation progress queue.
supervision.readiness: Complete outcome plus successful worker exit required before Load response.
supervision.unexpected_exit: An error; no incomplete response is loaded.

cases: A real 30,000-microvillus CPU worker finishes a 150 ms recording with no progress reader; the dialog reads the outcome after exit and enables loading.
The selected test clip is moved before preparation; the worker saves FileNotFoundError details, the dialog shows the error, and loading remains disabled.

checks: native preparation runs separately with progress while body and brain stay at time zero
prepared IDs, intensities, photons, channels and voltage match the previous offline recording exactly
native loader selects prepared sources at time zero with a video preview and real OpenGL brain
pause and release freeze brain, body, receptor clock and frame without resetting neural voltage
recording endpoint pauses exactly, with zero source/relay spikes and synchronized body and brain clocks
native full-brain final voltages and counts match the offline replay exactly
Reset clears the recording, source clamps and graded mode and restores normal video controls

limits: The previously stalled native attempt was not reproduced. Removing queue dependency and adding cancel/error supervision do not establish its original cause.
Two focused ordinary worker cases, one cancel during GPU startup, and one full Linux source-app preparation/playback workflow; no stress matrix.
Measured cancellation is one observation, not a universal stop-time guarantee. Termination still depends on OS/driver process handling.
A forcibly stopped worker can leave its last progress snapshot; its status file is not a live process monitor after the dialog closes.
Preparation equations, input rates, random streams, time steps and release assumptions are unchanged; physiological calibration remains unfinished.
No packaged-build or macOS/Windows supervision check.
